posts.name: Matthew McHale
posts.cooked:
Last night, we were playing against Ambuscade in... Time Cataclysm? I don't remember, but there was some environment effect that played the top card of the villain deck.

 

Ambuscade was flipped into cloaked mode, with the Personal Cloaking Device in play. Across the players' turns, we were able to destroy the cloaking device, but Ambuscade doesn't flip back until the villain turn. 

 

On the environment turn, a card was played that caused the top of the villain deck to be played, which was a card that said to search the villain deck and trash and put the Personal Cloaking Device in play. When it comes into play, the Personal Cloaking Device says to flip Ambuscade, which resulted in the cloaking device being in play and Ambuscade being on his "A side" (where his damage isn't prevented.)

 

Is there an official ruling/errata on what to do when this happens? We let Ambuscade stay in cloaked mode, but I'm pretty sure there are multiple environments that have effects that play the top card of the villain deck, so this could come up in other situations as well.

posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked:
Ironic:

Or, really, it should just make him immune to damage like a Mobile Defense Platform, and then he could have a real flip side.

His flip side doesn't just offer immunity to damage, though.  It changes him from targeting the highest-HP with projectile damage to targeting the lowest-HP with energy damage, and on advanced it makes all his damage irreducible.  Very much better suited to the idea of him stealthily stalking prey, rather than just blasting with guns out in the open.  (Though I might have made it melee damage rather than energy, as that's not very stealthy.)

posts.cooked: I don't mind Haka. Jim is very cool - I played him a lot after Shattered Timelines came out, though I like Omni-10 too :). My favourite hero is the Adept, but since Vengeance has come out the Naturalist is up there too. I like magic-based heroes who are really versatile and sort-of complicated so that you can always do something with them, regardless of what cards you have in-hand (admittedly the Adept isn't great if you have no songs, but since just under half his deck consists of songs, it's not too hard to get hold of one even if you're unlucky enough not to start with one in-hand ;)). Sometimes, though, I do just like to burn/smash/destroy stuff - so I'll take Ra or Jim or someone :D.
